clue.text: Beam from expert having trapped opponent

indicators.note: having trapped says the word for expert holds the word for opponent inside it

parts.note: an expert is clever, skilled
anti is someone opposed, an opponent

explanation.surface: A beam supplied by a specialist who has cornered a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam supported at only one end, as in bridges and balconies.

clue.text: Journalist, endlessly rigorous, covering syndicate

indicators.note: covering says the trimmed word wraps around the word for syndicate
endlessly says the word for rigorous loses its final letter

parts.note: stern means strict, rigorous
a ring is a group or syndicate working together

explanation.surface: A reporter, relentlessly thorough, investigating a crime syndicate.
explanation.walkthrough: A stringer is a freelance on retainer, not staff; 'endlessly' cuts the last letter, and 'covering' sets the ring word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringer is a freelance journalist paid per piece by a paper, rather than a staff reporter.

clue.text: Feign concern

definitions.meaning: to pretend or put on a show of a feeling
to have an effect on, involve or matter to

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to put on a manner falsely, and to touch or influence something.

clue.text: Musical with final character getting up and singing

indicators.note: getting up, in a down clue, says a letter rises from the bottom to the top of the word

parts.note: Cats is the Lloyd Webber musical
the final character of the musical's name is its last letter

explanation.surface: A stage show where the last performer stands up and starts to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' lifts the last letter S of CATS to the front in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is jazz vocalising with improvised nonsense syllables in place of words.

clue.text: Cleric showing care had worked with prisoner

indicators.note: worked says these letters are kneaded into a new order

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows compassion through his work with an inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' is the anagram signal on 'care had'; 'showing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican priest ranking just below a bishop.

clue.text: Father with great potting routine coming up with a break

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: potting suggests putting something into a pot, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: ace means excellent, great

indicators.note: coming up, in a down clue, says the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A snooker-playing priest whose fine potting routine leads to a big break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' and 'potting' suggest snooker, but potting means putting one piece inside another; 'coming up' turns only the routine word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is a crack or break, especially in a bone.

clue.text: Ruler, in trouble after exploit, left in exile

indicators.note: after places the word for trouble behind the trimmed word
in exile says that letter is sent away from the word

parts.note: to milk is to exploit someone or something
ado is fuss, bother, trouble

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch, facing trouble after a coup, is left to live abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in exile' removes the left letter; 'in trouble' is not a container, 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The mikado was the title used abroad for the Emperor of Japan.

clue.text: Look at hole with bend in fairway, ignoring peripheral features

indicators.note: ignoring peripheral features says the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: a golf hole whose fairway bends sharply is a dogleg

explanation.surface: A golfer studies a tricky hole that bends, paying no attention to the rough at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first and last letters of DOGLEG leaves the four in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone with obvious, lecherous interest.

clue.text: Mechanic in charge during over with half of race over

annotationWithheld.why: Mechanic in charge during over with half of race over: ARTIFICER needs IC inside ARTIFER, which reverses REFIT + RA; the printed first 'over' cannot give REFIT (perhaps 'overhaul' cut short), and no scan or search gives the full clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Mechanic in charge during over with half of race over

clue.text: Regretting decision to have learner expelled

indicators.note: expelled says the learner letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a ruling is an official decision
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A school regrets its decision to expel a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing means feeling sorrow or remorse over something.

clue.text: Relieved to be in shelter with weapon

indicators.note: to be in says the word for relieved sits inside the word for shelter

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter
relieved of something is rid of it

explanation.surface: Someone is glad to reach a refuge, armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relieved' looks like the surface's emotion but stands for RID, as in rid of a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, the weapon of Neptune.

clue.text: Man with anxiety about temperature in area

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: about says the word for anxiety goes around the temperature letter

parts.note: care means worry, anxiety

explanation.surface: A man frets about the heat in his neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of land area, ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: Authorised run

explanation.definitionFit: Legit is slang for legitimate or lawful; split in two it is the idiom for running off.

clue.text: Naive socialist arrested by copper, poor soul

indicators.note: arrested by says the policeman word holds the socialist word

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a red is a socialist or communist

indicators.note: poor says these letters are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gullible leftie is picked up by a policeman, the poor thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU; 'poor' shuffles SOUL to LOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Credulous means too ready to believe things, gullible.

clue.text: Appeal to receive one million altogether unlawfully

indicators.note: to receive says the appeal word takes the others inside it

parts.note: a cry is an appeal or plea
I is the Roman numeral one
in all means altogether, in total

explanation.surface: A plea to pocket a million in one go, illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminally means in a way that breaks the law.

clue.text: Planner, say, stopped by resistance over main point

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, puts the first part above the second
stopped by says the resistance letter plugs the word for say

parts.note: to say is to state
R is the physics symbol for resistance
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A planner is held up by opposition to the core of their scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist devises long-term plans, especially in war or business.

clue.text: Plant right beside trap that's covering area skirted by snake

indicators.note: skirted by says all these pieces sit inside the word for snake

parts.note: a viper is a venomous snake, such as the adder

indicators.note: beside sets the right letter next to the trap word

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap

indicators.note: covering says the that-is letters wrap around the word for area

parts.note: that's, as in that is, is i.e. (id est)
an acre is an area of land

explanation.surface: Instructions for a garden: a plant by the trap, covering ground fenced off by a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for i.e., id est; the snake's name is split open, with its first two letters before the long run and its last three after.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a climbing vine famous for its red autumn leaves.

clue.text: Minded about policy embraced by trendy director

indicators.note: embraced by says those letters sit inside the outer pair

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
C is short for circa, about
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A trendy director keen on a particular policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The trendy word and director letter form the outer pair, split around the about-and-policy run.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined means disposed or minded to do something.

clue.text: See nit dry up, ordered to give expert opinion

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Watch the louse dry out, as instructed, to give an expert's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges NIT, DRY and UP; 'See' and 'to give' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: Punditry is the giving of opinions by commentators and experts.

clue.text: Cut player's ending training, lacking heart

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of player's
lacking heart says the central letter of the word for training is dropped

parts.note: education is training, schooling

explanation.surface: A player is dropped, having stopped training, with no spirit left.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of EDUCATION is its fifth letter, A, which goes; R from player's goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a cut, a decrease in amount.

clue.text: Teacher going over set of answers for bonehead

indicators.note: going over, in a down clue, puts the teacher word above the next

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
a key is a list of answers to a test or puzzle

explanation.surface: A teacher marks a dunce's test against the answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey is a slang insult for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Artist from north with backing group going around

indicators.note: going around says the reversed word wraps the north letter
backing says the word for group is read backwards

parts.note: a team is a group

explanation.surface: A painter from up north tours with his support band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns TEAM into MAET, and 'going around' puts N inside: MA-N-ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard Manet was the French painter of Olympia and Le Dejeuner sur l'herbe.

clue.text: Language used by Roman churchmen

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken by Catholic clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language' and 'Roman churchmen' invite Latin, but the letters sit inside romAN CHUrchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchu is the Tungusic tongue of the Manchus, the people who founded the Qing dynasty.

clue.text: Bar to be twisted in an act

indicators.note: to be twisted says the letters that follow are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A bar is to be wrecked during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a bar or tavern in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Cover matter under investigation

definitions.meaning: a box or sheath that protects something
a crime or legal matter being looked into

explanation.definitionFit: A pillowcase or briefcase holds and protects; a detective works on a criminal inquiry.

clue.text: Unsettled, getting pressure before reaching conclusion

indicators.note: before puts the pressure letter ahead of the next word

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Negotiations remain open, with pressure growing before a deal is reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Pending means awaiting a decision, not yet resolved.

clue.text: Declared full agreement

indicators.note: declared says the word is spoken, so we hear its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: packed means full, crammed

explanation.surface: A complete accord is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement or treaty.

clue.text: A riddle? That's Ballesteros, hooking one

indicators.note: hooking says the golfer's name catches the one letter inside it

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was the Spanish golfer, known by his first name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A puzzle: is that the famous golfer slicing, or rather hooking, a shot?
explanation.walkthrough: A riddle is also a coarse sieve, used to sift soil or gravel; 'riddle' wants to mean a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle in its gardening sense is a large coarse sifting tool.

clue.text: Navy, small, led by king with hope initially in crazy fight

indicators.note: led by puts the following pieces ahead of the navy and small letters
in says the king letter and the hope letter go inside the word for crazy

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of hope

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A small navy, under a king who has hope, launches a mad attack.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'led by' puts the king-hope-crazy block in front of the navy and small letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock horns is to clash or fight, like stags with their antlers locked.
